task.description:
Write the tests of REQ-070 (WF-02 step 5). The data is built (step 05) and passed the security and review gates (steps 06, 07). Read: the design docs/design/REQ-070-demo-tenants-v3.md in full (sections 6-12 are yours: the table of 21 tests DT-1a...DT-7b, the literals of 8.3, the mutants MU in 12, the guard replacement table in 9 which is empty), the block REQ-070 in docs/requirements.yaml with its seven criteria, decisions 0086, 0085, the step 02 and 04 results (the gate's Low findings P1-P4), the data files tools/src/picker/demo-tenants-v3/*.json and demo-answers-v3/*.json, the sample docs/design/samples/picker-v3-approved-2026-10-26/data.js, the test style of tools/test/picker-look.test.js, picker-look-helpers.js (imported, never changed), picker-server.test.js.
Write exactly one new test file tools/test/picker-demo-v3.test.js with the 21 tests of the design (the ids as in 8.2), and change nothing else in the project (no data, no src, no other tests; if a test cannot be written without a helper, put the helper inside the test file). Rules: independent oracles (own contrast function with the literals #f3f5f9 and #161f2e, literals for expected compositions, the sample loaded as a module with a substituted window and compared by the path map), no import of the checked functions to compute an expected value (imports only to call them), no fixed port (--port 0), a temporary home folder for serve, everything cleaned up, no clock, no order dependence, no skip or todo. Add what the gate asked: P1 — DT-1b pins the `when` conditions of the rules and the hypotheses (not only ids and points), and add to the mutants you run two of your own kinds: move a boundary of a rule's number condition and change a hypothesis' budget condition; P3 — the attribution of MU30 includes DT-2c; P4(b) — DT-6b may repeat the six questionnaire hashes (pinned by the design) but state in a comment that a later requirement changes both places. DT-2d needs the second sample tenant (the two roles equal word for word in both sample tenants). DT-3a pins only the SHAPE of `half` (the engine refuses it today).
Mutants: apply every MU of section 12 and your own two, one at a time, on a scratch copy of tools/ (session scratchpad folder named in the launching message; restore the file from the live tree after each run; sequentially, --test-concurrency=1; no git checkout/reset/stash/clean, also not in scratch copies); each must turn at least one test red; report equivalent mutants with a reason; put the table (mutant, killing tests, count of failing tests) in result.self_check. Then `cd tools && npm run check` once: zero red, the number of tests = 2044 + 21 (unless the design says another); format:check, lint, traces and handoffs-check green; the sha256 of the sorted per-file sha256 list of tools/src and the data folders equal at start and end. Real defects of the data found by the tests stay red and are reported (do not fix the data; do not weaken a test). In your handoff text never list project names or machine paths (say "the traces list"). 16 GB RAM computer: single commands, one run at a time.

result.summary:
One new test file, tools/test/picker-demo-v3.test.js, with the 21 tests DT-1a...DT-7b of the design (4+4+3+4+1+3+2). All 21 are green on the data as built (steps 05-07); no real defect of the data was found, so nothing stays red. Oracles are independent: an own contrast function and HSL with the literal sheets #f3f5f9 and #161f2e; literal tables for the composition, the 15+15 rules with their conditions, the hypotheses, the outcomes and the old-stand hashes; the approved sample loaded with vm and a substituted window and compared through a path map; the sample is copied through JSON so that deep comparison works; a second scoring over the literal rule table. The checked code is only called (the real check command, the real check function, the real engine, the real view of a file, the real serve command). serve runs with port 0, a temporary home folder (env HOME and --home) and is stopped by SIGTERM; every temporary folder is removed by the helper; no clock, no random, no order dependence, no skip, no todo, no rule turned off; no helper file and no shared helper changed (helpers only imported).
Criterion -> test (Q5): 1 (check passes, composition, 8 colours, replacements, the rule bites) -> DT-1a, DT-1b, DT-1c, DT-1d; 2 (three languages, truthful intro, ru = sample except the table, reasons) -> DT-2a, DT-2b, DT-2c, DT-2d; 3 (outcomes of the sets) -> DT-3a, DT-3b, DT-3c; 4 (separate files) -> DT-4a, DT-4b, DT-4c, DT-4d; 5 (reader) -> the BA-ANALYST step, DT-5a pins the counts of rows the reader's table must hold; 6 (new stand and old stand) -> DT-6a, DT-6b, DT-6c; 7 (invented data, nothing extra) -> DT-7a, DT-7b (the commands npm run traces, npm run check and the test( count loop are run by RELEASE-VALIDATOR and TEST-RUNNER; the git diff of criterion 6 is run-relative and is not a standing test, design 8.4).
What was added for the gate remarks: P1 - DT-1b pins the `when` conditions of all 30 rules and the 4 hypotheses (an any_of list is compared sorted, min and max exactly), and DT-3c scores every combination of the single answers (stock 144 x 9 numbers, agency 144 x 8 numbers, numbers at the edges of the rules) a second time with the literal rule table and compares totals, order, recommended, clear leader, fired rules and hypotheses with the real engine; two own kinds of mutant were run (OM1 a boundary of a number condition, OM3 a budget condition of a hypothesis) plus two more (OM4, OM5), all killed by DT-1b and DT-3c. P3 - the attribution of MU30 includes DT-2c: confirmed by the run (DT-2c, DT-4b). P4(b) - DT-6b repeats the six questionnaire hashes; a comment in the test says that a later requirement that changes the old stand on purpose changes both places (this test and SV-9 of the server tests). DT-2d reads the second sample tenant (the roles of desk 1 and desk 4 are equal word for word in both sample tenants and equal the `was` texts of E2 and E3), and E1 is not asked for it. DT-3a pins only the shape of `half`; the test does not run the engine on `half` (what the engine does with it is REQ-072's).
Quality-bar items: Q8 - DT-4a (ids), DT-4b (every visitor string in ru, kk and en, folded, no common element), DT-4c (colours), DT-4d (a broken neighbour does not change the check; folder unchanged), plus MU17, MU18, MU30 kill; Q10 - the data calls nothing external; the failure case that exists is a broken file or a broken neighbour: DT-4d (code 0 for the good file, the broken one gives code 1, no file written), DT-1d (the check refuses a bad colour with one line, no file written); Q11 - not applicable, the data holds no address (DT-7a shows it, MU22a and MU22b kill); R3 - not applicable (decision 0033); Q7 - no secret in the test, the two whatsapp numbers are the invented numbers of the requirement; Q9 - no SQL; R2 - Pixel Office not touched.
Evidence that the tests catch (WF-02: no copy with broken code, so mutants): the design's MU1...MU30 and four of my own were applied one at a time; each turned at least one test red, none is equivalent; the table is in self_check. Differences from the design's Seen-by column are only additions (a mutant is also seen by tests the design did not list, for example MU12 by DT-3c, MU19 by DT-3c, MU24 by DT-7a), and MU29 is seen only by DT-2d, as the design says.

issues.text: No code edit is needed and no real defect of the data was found: every literal of the design matched the built files on the first run. The only reds while writing were three sanity floors of my own on the number of texts and ids; they were lowered to counts that the files hold (the floors only guard against an emptied file).

Two comparison details a reader may ask about: (a) an any_of list in the file is compared sorted with the design's list (the order of the options inside a condition has no meaning for the engine), while min, max, ids, points and the order of rules are compared exactly; (b) the number of mapped texts of the path map is pinned (stock 32, agency 33) so that the sample comparison cannot become empty.

The old-stand literals (the six questionnaire hashes) are now written in two test files (this one and the server tests, SV-9). The comment in the test says that a later requirement that changes the old stand on purpose edits both places (gate remark P4 b).
The number of tests is 2044 + 21 = 2065; the run gave 2065. The owner's servers on ports 4782 and 4790 were not touched; this step started no process that is still running.
